suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-30 adds this relationship only as a bounded sleep-disorder association. Sleep abnormalities including insomnia-type complaints are documented across the clinical stages of Alzheimer disease in systematic review and network meta-analysis evidence, but the primary diagnosis alone does not establish an insomnia disorder in every person or determine an individual's sleep course. Require independently documented Alzheimer disease, objectively documented insomnia disorder by validated sleep assessment compatible in chronology, and specialist review. Preserve depression, anxiety, obstructive sleep apnea, medications, other neurodegenerative disease, and primary sleep disorders as competing causes of disturbed sleep.

sourceReferences.citation: Zhang Y, Ren R, Feng X, Wang M, Huang J, Shi J, Lu L, Sanford LD, Vitiello MV, Tang X. Sleep abnormalities across different clinical stages of Alzheimer's disease: A systematic review and network meta-analysis. Sleep Med Rev. 2026;88:102289. PMID 41985272. doi:10.1016/j.smrv.2026.102289.
sourceReferences.note: Systematic review and network meta-analysis characterizing sleep abnormalities, including insomnia-type disturbances, across the Alzheimer disease clinical continuum. It supports a bounded disease-association proposition and clinical evaluation, not automatic individual causation or aggravation.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 41985272; stage-stratified sleep abnormality synthesis across the AD continuum

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Sleep abnormalities are consistently documented across Alzheimer disease stages, but review and meta-analytic evidence does not establish an individual medical nexus without documentation of both the neurodegenerative disease and the insomnia disorder, compatible chronology, and competing-cause review.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR § 3.310 is established by this association evidence; the mapping is not an individual nexus opinion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Neurodegenerative disruption of circadian and sleep-regulating hypothalamic and brainstem networks is hypothesized to fragment sleep and reduce sleep continuity in Alzheimer disease, but the individual pathway must be established from sleep studies, cognitive-stage documentation, and specialist evaluation.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Sleep abnormalities are documented across the Alzheimer disease continuum in systematic review evidence, but that evidence does not establish that AD caused or aggravated an insomnia disorder in every individual; both diagnoses, chronology, objective sleep findings, and competing etiologies require case-specific review.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented AD and insomnia disorder; chronology; polysomnographic or validated sleep findings; depression, apnea, medication, and primary sleep disorder alternatives; specialist assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Depression, anxiety, and other psychiatric causes of insomnia
Obstructive sleep apnea and other primary sleep disorders
Sedating or stimulating medication effects and other neurodegenerative disease
